content.thinking:
I'm planning the layout for the shrine scene without testing the code directly—positioning a small hokora shrine, a roadside torii gate, and stone lanterns around a stone slab base, working out their relative placements and sizes.

For details I'm adding an offerings table with a sake barrel, bowls, and fruit, plus a shimenawa rope with shide paper cards, keeping the fox statue idea but skipping anything too elaborate. I'm reviewing the builder API available to me—box, part, rod, lathe, extrude helpers—and thinking through how to render the shide cards as thin double-sided planes since using the frame helper feels risky without testing.

I'm settling on using boxes with textures for the shide ofuda since box geometry shows texture on all faces cleanly. I'm also capping the color palette to keep things modest, using cel-shaded paints for vermilion, wood, stone, gold, and cream, and defining helper functions for boxes and cylinders to build the torii's pillars and curved kasagi top beam, deciding on black for the kasagi and vermilion for the nuki crossbeam.

Now I'm planning the plaque with simple drawn shapes instead of relying on fonts, adding hanging paper lanterns along the nuki beam positioned at specific heights, and sketching out a stone lantern (toro) with a hexagonal base, pillar, glowing firebox window, roof, and jewel top using lathe geometry.

Simplifying the firebox glow to a cube body with two crossing boxes creating glow slits on all four sides, then moving on to designing the hexagonal lathe profile for the roof shape.

For the hokora shrine, I'm planning a stone step base with a small vermilion-pillared wooden building, lattice doors, and working out the gable roof as an extruded triangular profile along the depth axis.

Working out the roof panel geometry—placing each sloped panel at the right x-offset with a 28° tilt rotated oppositely on each side so they angle downward away from the ridge, with a gold ridge rod and a dark teal striped tile texture for the roof color.

Now I'm layering in the shrine details: a sagging shimenawa rope with hanging zigzag shide paper, an offering table stacked with sake barrel, rice bowls, orange fruit, mochi, incense burner, candle, and fan, plus tokkuri bottles, a slatted wooden coin box scattered with gold coins, and a pair of stone kitsune fox statues with capsule bodies, cone ears, and red bibs flanking the shrine steps.

I'm positioning the toro lanterns, foxes, and a stone-slab path leading up to the torii, scattering a few flat pink petal shapes on the ground, and considering a floating glowing orb before deciding instead to add a glowing rune circle decal on the ground near the torii for a magical touch.

Still working out the spatial layout...

With platform width 3.6, I'll place the offering table at x=-1.4, a sake barrel stack at x=1.45, and add some grass clumps and hydrangea-like sphere clusters at the corners for greenery. The torii height comes to about 2.75 total. Now I'm setting up the toon cel color palette for vermillion, wood, and darker accent tones before writing the actual construction code.

Setting up more cel colors and a lathe helper function...

Designing the torii gate structure now: tapered pillar lathes, dark base rings with stone footing, and the kasagi/nuki crossbeams with gold end caps positioned above the pillars.

I'm adding the shimaki and plaque details between the crossbeams, with an SVG texture for the plaque showing a dark background, gold border, and a circle-and-lines symbol. Now I'm starting on the hanging paper lantern using a lathe shape for its glowing form.

Still writing lathe geometry...

For the lantern details I'm adding gold caps top and bottom, a rope attachment to the nuki, and thin dark torus rings around the body to suggest ribs, skipping a painted texture since the glow material can't take stripes.

For the ground I'm generating a cyan rune circle texture with radial strokes to place on the platform beneath the torii, plus a stone platform with curb edging and paver boxes forming a path from the torii to the steps.

I'm adjusting paver placement so they flank the rune circle without overlapping it, spacing a couple along each side plus near the steps. Now I'm starting a fox statue function that builds the body from scaled spheres for haunches and chest, with cylinder legs, facing forward and angled slightly inward.

I'm continuing the fox details: head and snout shapes, cone ears, a curled tail swept with a spline, a red bib torus at the neck, and a small pedestal base, composed through local offset helpers so everything mirrors symmetrically. I'm setting the stone-gray statue material with a red cel-shaded bib, dark eye spheres, and a small gold bell.

Now I'm planning the shrine offerings in front of the steps — a tray with rice bowls, sake cup, oranges, candles, and incense — plus an ema plaque rack to the side with textured wooden plaques.

I'm working out the layout positions: ema rack on the left front, barrels and offering table on the right front, carefully placing coordinates so nothing overlaps near the torii pillars. Then I'm sketching the hokora shrine structure itself — stone steps rising in stacked boxes up to a raised wooden deck, working out the y-heights so each step sits correctly on the one below.

Now I'm detailing the shrine building: vermilion pillars at the corners, dark wall panels, front doors with latticed red texture and gold studs, lighter wood side walls, an eave beam, and triangular gable ends extruded in wood tones at front and back, plus a gold ornamental chigi piece on top.

Working out the roof and ornaments: crossed rods at the ridge ends with a kagura bell and twisted red-white rope hanging in front, positioning the roof peak above the eave beam, calculating the overhang, and placing the bell near the saisen offering box in front of the steps.

I'm checking the saisen box and step placements don't collide with the path pavers, adjusting z-depths so the box sits just past the steps, then positioning the hanging bell and its gently curving rope above it before moving on to the door transom detail.

Now I'm adding small glow lanterns at the shrine eave corners, reusing a scalable lantern-building function so each one is positioned and sized consistently from the eave edges inward. I'm also working out the shimenawa rope and paper shide zigzag strips hanging between the pillars, making sure their height doesn't clash with the nuki beam and plaque above.

Adding gold filigree accents at the torii end caps, nuki trim lines, roof ridge, and lantern sills for that genshin aesthetic. I'll skip side torches but add bushes at the outer platform corners for greenery.

I'm also placing a small sakura tree behind the shrine around 2.2m tall, built from a curved trunk sweep with branch rods and clustered pink canopy spheres plus scattered petal boxes on the ground, keeping the triangle count well under 60k.

Now I'm planning the helper functions for building box, sphere, and lathe parts with consistent signatures for position, rotation, scale, color, and texture, making sure to avoid unused variable errors as I write the actual code.

Still building fox geometry...

Adding the eyes with a gold glow, a red bib with a torus collar and bell, then sweeping a curled tail that mirrors outward based on the character's side position for symmetry.

Now I'm designing the ema votive rack: wooden posts with a beam and small roofed top, hanging five tablets by cords, each textured with a sakura, fox, or star SVG design shown on all faces, arranged across the beam with slight rotations.

For the ema shape itself, I'm building a pentagon-cut wood plaque with a gable roofline by making the corners transparent via a polygon mask, plus a wood fill, border, picture area, and red tassel. Then I'm sketching a sake barrel using a lathe profile that bulges outward in the middle before tapering back in.

I'm adding wood grain texture, gold-dark hoops and straw rope around the barrel, plus a labeled front panel with a white background and red stripe, positioned using a plane geometry. I'm planning two floor barrels and a smaller one stacked on top, then starting on an offering table with a wooden tabletop and legs positioned to hold items above the floor.

For items on the table, I'm sketching lathe-turned sake cups, a rice bowl with a white mound, oranges on a small sanbo stand, and a kagami mochi made from two flattened spheres topped with an orange. I'm also adding a glowing candle flame, extra offering bowls on the steps, and a bronze tripod incense censer with ash and three glowing incense sticks near the front. Now I'm ready to move into writing the actual code, keeping it thorough but not overly elaborate.

Writing the tree code with a sweep-based trunk using a bark texture paint, then scattering spheres around the canopy center to form hydrangea-pink foliage clusters with varied colors and sizes...

Adding scattered falling petal boxes with random rotations across the platform area, then defining the base platform geometry with a bordered curb strip around its edges...

Still writing platform styling...

Now I'm planning the SVG assets: a cyan rune with thick strokes, a torii door with vermilion background, gold frame and lattice lines, and a simple barrel label with a red band and black emblem. Time to start coding these pieces.
